title: Appointment No-Show Recovery Bench
oneLiner: A small-service operator console that turns missed appointments into deposits, waitlist offers, and polite recovery scripts.
targetUser: Salon, clinic, repair, tutoring, coaching, and consultation businesses that lose revenue to no-shows.
keyUx: Choose a service type and no-show pattern; the bench recommends deposit size, confirmation timing, waitlist fill actions, and customer-safe wording.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web prototype for "Appointment No-Show Recovery Bench". Target user: small appointment-based operators such as salons, clinics, tutors, repair services, and coaches. Core UX: the operator reviews recent missed appointments, selects service value and customer relationship risk, and receives a deposit policy, confirmation cadence, waitlist recovery action, and polite SMS scripts. Required sections: compact no-show queue, lost revenue counter, policy simulator, script variants, waitlist replacement lane, and weekly policy notes. Use the operator-dense design profile: disciplined B2B console styling, compact rows, tabular numbers, one sharp action accent, no decorative hero, and crisp queue/table hierarchy.

sourceSignals.source: Reddit r/smallbusiness: reducing no-shows for service appointments
sourceSignals.evidence: Service operators ask whether reminders, deposits, confirmations, cancellation policies, or fees actually reduce no-shows.
sourceSignals.action: Owners test SMS reminders, small deposits, and waitlist recovery manually.

sourceSignals.source: Reddit r/smallbusiness: whether charging no-show deposits feels rude
sourceSignals.evidence: Owners worry the policy that protects revenue may make them look rude or greedy.
sourceSignals.action: They ask peers for wording, deposit size, and cancellation policy norms.
